about: Generated tables of docs/benchmarks.md, rendered by docs/scripts/render_benchmarks.py. 'runs' holds the consolidated EC2 runs: 'label' and 'rows' are copied from each run folder's consolidated.json, 'chain' from the end-to-end table of its CONSOLIDATED.md (with en dashes and ×), 'source' is the folder in this repository and 'caption' is the short name the page prints. 'more' holds runs outside the consolidated benchmark, all in the Docker VM ('more_label'), each group with its own source. 'tables' holds hand-entered tables with columns of their own (the WARC runs), each with its caption and source. Units: microseconds per document (rows; pyroid_us is one thread on CPython 3.15t, pyroid_us_8_threads a pool of 8, incumbents one process on CPython 3.13) and seconds per run (chain). Every value is a string copied from the source, never computed.

more_label: Docker/OrbStack VM on Apple Silicon (12 vCPU), indicative

more.title: pyroid.metrics: ROUGE, BLEU and chrF
more.note: Milliseconds for the whole workload, median of the runs (a single run for the reference libraries on 100k pairs). Every row was first checked identical to the 1-process reference. The reference libraries ran in 1 process and in 8 forked processes, pyroid in one process with threads=1 and threads=8. CPython 3.13, release wheel; other work kept the load average between 4 and 19. ROUGE scores CNN/DailyMail lead-3 against the highlights with rouge1/2/L/Lsum (the 100k pairs are the 11,490 pairs repeated). BLEU and chrF use WMT21 segments, the first reference and default settings.

more.title: pyroid.json_repair
more.note: Single documents, best time per call, json_repair 0.64.5 on CPython 3.12 (3.15t was within ±10%). Release wheel; other work kept the load average between 16 and 24.

more.title: pyroid.json_repair: batches
more.note: Documents per second over 10,000 broken documents of about 1.2 KB, on free-threaded CPython 3.15t with the GIL off. The shared, loaded VM limits the 8-thread rows.

more.title: pyroid.yaml
more.label: AWS EC2 c7i.4xlarge (Intel Xeon Sapphire Rapids, 16 vCPU), dedicated, nothing else running
more.note: MB/s of YAML read (loads) or written (dumps), one process at a time, each cell in a fresh one, CPython 3.12.16 with PyYAML 6.0.3 and libyaml 0.2.5; load average at most 1.07 (the benchmark itself). The corpus is the 11,878 files of the parity corpus that PyYAML loads (343 MB); the 1, 10 and 100 MB files concatenate real ones.
more.footnote: For context, on the same inputs: ruamel.yaml 0.19.1's pure-Python safe loader 0.65, 1.02, 0.78 and 0.72 MB/s; with ruamel.yaml.clib 0.2.15, 3.20 and 7.42 MB/s on the corpus and the 1 MB file (42 corpus files and the 10 and 100 MB files raise); rapidyaml 0.15.2's `parse_in_arena`, which builds a parse tree but no Python objects, 156, 202, 167 and 112 MB/s (66 corpus files raise). ruamel.yaml reads YAML 1.2, so its results differ from PyYAML's.

more.title: pyroid.yaml: small documents
more.label: AWS EC2 c7i.4xlarge (Intel Xeon Sapphire Rapids, 16 vCPU), dedicated, nothing else running
more.note: Time per call, best of 7 rounds interleaved in one process; the 2 KB document is a GitHub Actions workflow.

more.title: pyroid.datasketch: MinHash signatures
more.note: Seconds for the first 10,000 FineWeb dev documents (5.1 million word 5-gram shingles), 128 permutations, best of 3, on free-threaded CPython 3.15t with the GIL off. datasketch 2.0.0 with numpy 2.5.4; its 8-thread rows split the documents over a thread pool. Every pyroid result was first checked for identical signatures. Load average 7 to 10.

more.title: pyroid.datasketch: MinHashLSH
more.note: Milliseconds for 10,000 affine32 signatures, 128 permutations, same run. The loop rows call insert or query per document with LeanMinHash objects; the batch rows pass the signature matrix. Every query result set was first checked against datasketch's.

more.title: pyroid.jieba
more.note: µs per document over 1,000 FineWeb-2 cmn_Hani documents (the slice four times, about 1,450 characters each), on free-threaded CPython 3.15t with the GIL off, release wheel, median of 5 runs (2 for jieba), load average 1.5 to 3. Every document's words were first checked against jieba 0.42.1's. jieba's 8 processes are a warmed fork Pool(8); its 8 threads run in parallel on 3.15t.
more.footnote: pyroid builds the Python lists of words on the calling thread (about 35 µs per document), which limits the 8-thread rows. A fresh interpreter reaches its first segmented sentence in 27 ms with pyroid (import included) and about 410 ms with jieba.

more.title: pyroid.nltk
more.note: µs per document over the first 1,000 documents of the FineWeb dev slice (3,018 characters each on average), English model, release wheels, median of 5 runs (2 for NLTK), load average 3 to 5. Every document's output was first checked against NLTK 3.10.4's. NLTK's 8 processes are a warmed fork Pool(8); its 8 threads run in parallel only on 3.15t.
more.footnote: Speedups are against NLTK on one thread. pyroid builds the Python lists of sentences and tokens on the calling thread, which limits the 8-thread rows; against NLTK on 8 processes they are 35× (sent_tokenize) and 14× (word_tokenize) on 3.13. The first sentence in a fresh interpreter takes 177 ms with pyroid and 203 ms with NLTK on 3.13: pyroid imports NLTK to find the model when NLTK is installed.

more.title: pyroid.trafilatura
more.note: Milliseconds per page over 1,000 pages of the CC-MAIN-2026-39 development sample (157,000 characters each on average), CPython 3.13, release wheel, load average 2 to 4. Each mode against its own trafilatura release, with lxml 6.1.3 and jusText 3.0.2, and every page's text first checked identical. datatrove's call is `favor_precision=True, include_comments=False, deduplicate=True`; with dedup, pages are extracted in page order, so threads only parse ahead.

more.source: the trafilatura port's timing runs on 2026-11-09, whose scripts are not in the repository

more.title: Languages: FineWeb-2 filters and MinHash
more.note: µs per document over 1,000 documents per language (each FineWeb-2 slice four times), median of 5 runs (2 for datatrove). Every timed document was first checked for the same keep/drop, reason and signatures. The filters are FineWeb-2's chain (Gopher repetition, FineWeb quality, Gopher quality) with each language's settings; MinHash computes FineWeb-2's signatures. datatrove's 8 processes are a warmed fork Pool(8). CPython 3.13, release wheel, load average 6 to 16.
more.footnote: \* An outlier: in this run pyroid was slower with 8 threads than with 1 while the load rose. It needs a rerun before it can be quoted. † Rerun on 2026-11-07 with the native Chinese tokenizer (pyroid.jieba), load average 1 to 2; through python_tokenizer=True it had run at 1.2× / 0.9× on one thread and 0.4× with 8. ‡ Rerun on 2026-11-09 with the native Japanese tokenizer (a port of SudachiPy 0.7.0, sudachidict-core 20261015), load average 0.6 to 1.9; through python_tokenizer=True it had run at 1.2× / 0.9× on one thread and 0.3× / 0.2× with 8. SudachiPy's lattice dominates both sides: pyroid's whole MinHash (1,151 µs per document, one thread) takes less than SudachiPy's own tokenize() on the same chunks (1,583 µs). § Measured on 2026-11-09 with the native Vietnamese tokenizer (a port of pyvi 0.1.1 through spaCy) and the native Thai one (a port of PyThaiNLP 5.4.0, reading the installed pythainlp's word list and model), load average 2.1 at the start and 7.4 after the 8-worker runs. Through python_tokenizer=True, before the ports, they ran at 1.5× / 1.5× (Vietnamese) and 1.5× / 1.6× (Thai) on one thread, and 0.4× / 0.2× and 0.6× / 0.7× with 8; that run overlapped other builds on the VM (load average 3.5 to 23), so only its ratios are given.

more.title: More datatrove steps
more.note: Each datatrove step alone on the FineWeb dev slice, in one process and in a warmed multiprocessing.Pool(8), against pyroid's native call at 1 and 8 threads. Medians of 5 runs for pyroid and 2 for datatrove; release wheel, CPython 3.13, taskset -c 0-7, load average about 8 (about 22 for the URL filter). Where datatrove wasn't measured at 8 processes, the 8-thread speedup is against one process.
more.source: a one-off run on 2026-11-06, whose scripts are not in the repository

more.title: datatrove's FineWeb pipeline with pyroid's steps swapped in
more.note: Whole runs on the FineWeb dev slice (10,000 documents unless noted): wall seconds, and user+sys CPU seconds including children, from bash's `time`. CPython 3.13, release wheel, taskset -c 0-7. The VM was heavily shared (load average 18 to 30), which slows stock datatrove the most, so each ratio comes from a pair of runs in the same minute (stock, then pyroid). pyroid's runs include datatrove's executor phases, worker start-up, Parquet IO and loading the 125 MiB model; `pyroid clean` includes interpreter start-up, IO and writing both outputs. Every output has datatrove's per-document digest.

c7i-warc.caption: AWS EC2 c7i.4xlarge (Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, 16 vCPU), Amazon Linux 2023, every run on CPUs 0 to 7; CPython 3.13.18, datatrove 0.10.1 with trafilatura 1.11.0, and a pyroid release wheel built on the instance. 8 WARC files of CC-MAIN-2026-39 (7.5 GB, 171,595 HTML records), one task per file. Each run was timed once; fastest first. CPU s is user+sys including the worker processes. The Trafilatura column is the time datatrove's statistics give that step, summed over tasks.
